item.description:
- **Fixed:** CJ OnStyle's overseas hotel list showed "NaN원" as the price a night. The site reads its dates in a way only Chromium accepts (with a space at the end), so WebKit couldn't count the nights. Changmun now reads such a date the way Chromium does, on that site only.
Tried on the site's hotel list for Tokyo, and with automated tests. If another site shows "NaN" or a blank where a number should be and works in Chrome, tell me which.

- **New:** the address bar opens the site you mean. Type the start of a site you visit (`git`) and it comes first, with the rest of its name filled in, so Return opens github.com instead of searching. Keep typing over the filled-in part, or press Delete to search for what you typed. A name is filled in only into that site's own domain, so a page you were once redirected to can't stand in for github.com. - **New:** saved logins are offered right under the field when you click a username or password field, like other browsers do. The list is drawn by Changmun, not the page, so the page can't see which accounts you have. Filling still asks for Touch ID if you have that turned on. - **New:** logins are shared across one site's addresses (www., accounts., nid.naver.com…), labelled with the address they were saved for. Never across sites where each subdomain belongs to someone else (github.io, tistory.com and the rest of the Public Suffix List), and never for the AI's sign-in, which still needs the exact host. - **New:** File › Import Passwords from CSV File… reads exports from Apple's Passwords app, Chrome, Firefox, Bitwarden and 1Password. Only https logins are saved. When everything was saved, it offers to move the CSV, which holds your passwords in plain text, to the Trash. - **Fixed:** sites signed you out after you hadn't used them for a week. WebKit's tracking prevention erased what sites store for themselves; that erasing is now off, and the rest of tracking prevention, third-party cookie blocking included, stays on. - **Fixed:** the first click on a page after using another app only brought the window forward; it now reaches the page, as in Chrome. - **Fixed:** a page that was on its way to another site could be offered and filled with that site's saved login. Logins now go only to the page actually on screen.
Tried with automated tests. Whether week-old sign-ins now survive can only be seen after a week, so tell me if a site still signs you out.

- **Fixed:** a link that passes through an ad or tracking address on its way (an ad's or a newsletter's click tracker) stopped there instead of reaching the page it leads to. The ad and tracking lists now block only what pages load, not the page you go to; lists you added yourself still keep the window off their sites. The rules are rebuilt the next time you open Changmun. - **Fixed:** the AI couldn't read some pages, YouTube's among them, when a long name on the page had an emoji where it was cut; it reported that the page didn't answer in time.
Tried with automated tests on pages that do the same. The sites where links stopped haven't been tried, so tell me if one still does.

- **New:** when you type a search in the address bar, the other search engines in your list are offered under it. Click one, or press ⌘ and its number while the bar is open, to search with it just this once; your default engine stays as it is. - **New:** the search engines are one list in Settings › General › Search. Take any of them out (all but the default), and put engines in from Add Search Engine: one you took out, a well-known one (Daum, YouTube, Namuwiki, Wikipedia, Coupang, Naver Map, GitHub, Perplexity), or any other.
Tried with automated tests and the off-screen test copy.

- **Changed:** the AI button at the right of the bar now sits as far from the address as from the window's edge (18 pt each), instead of floating nearer the edge; the address is 8 pt wider.
Tried with automated tests and by measuring the bar of the off-screen test copy.

- **Added:** when a link or a button that should open a new tab does nothing, Changmun now leaves a line about it in the Mac's system log (Console, subsystem io.github.namekun.Changmun, category windows): what kind of click it was, whether it came from you, and what Changmun decided. It keeps only the site's name and a scrambled form of the page path, never the rest of the address, and writes nothing for private windows. It is there so that a link that sometimes does nothing, like Instagram's ad links did for a while, can be traced the next time it happens.
Tried with automated tests. The log lines themselves haven't been read back on another Mac.

- **Changed:** a favorite whose tab is playing sound, or is muted, now shows it as a small speaker badge on the tile's corner instead of a button laid over half the site's icon. Click the badge to mute or unmute, as before.
Tried with automated tests, including one that draws the tile and checks how much of the icon the speaker covers (a fifth before, under a tenth now).

A pass over the things only the person who wrote Changmun would know, and the habits you bring from other browsers.
- **Nothing lost without a word:** quitting asks while files still download; pages with unsaved changes ask before you leave; an AI question you don't answer in 90 seconds counts as Don't Allow and says so; Stop keeps the messages that were waiting; ⇧⌘T brings closed tabs back after a restart too (Clear History removes them). - **Moving around:** right-click ‹ or › for the page history, ⌘. or Esc to stop loading, ⌘← / ⌘→ to go back and forward when the page doesn't use those keys, ⌘R retries a page that failed, ⌥-click downloads a link, and Develop › View Page Source (⌥⌘U). - **Tabs:** ⌘⇧[ ⌘⇧] and ⌘1–9 follow the whole sidebar; middle-click closes a tab; Close Other Tabs and Close Tabs Below; Undo after closing a tab; Move to Space; a "…" menu on every tab row; favorites and bookmarks show and mute their sound. - **Said in words:** "Not Secure" on http pages, "Camera on" while a page uses it (click to stop), the AI button says Working or Answered with its panel closed, and sleeping or background tabs say so. - **Easier to find:** a Help menu with the guide and every shortcut (⌘/), Settings search that finds every setting, and a first-run screen that shows the search bar, spaces and approvals. - **New:** notifications when a download finishes or the AI waits while you're in another app, the download count on the Dock icon, Share and Services, your own search engines with a keyword, and bookmarks exported to or imported from an HTML file.
Tried with 1611 automated tests and the off-screen test copy. Dragging, hover and notification prompts were not tried on a real screen yet.

- **Changed:** when a page is waiting on you (a pop-up it was refused, a password to save, an extension to install), the left of the address now says so in words, such as "Pop-up Blocked", instead of showing a small dot that didn't say what it was. Press it for the same choices as before, such as "Always Allow for This Site".
Tried with automated tests and the off-screen test copy, on a page that opens an empty window from a timer the way older in-house systems do.

- **Fixed:** when a site opened an empty window without a click and filled it in itself, as many older in-house and school systems do, Changmun blocked it without telling you, so there was no way to let it through and the site just failed. Now the dot beside the address tells you about it, with "Always Allow for This Site"; allow it and press the site's button again.
Tried with automated tests on a page that opens an empty window from a timer. The in-house system this came up on hasn't been tried, so tell me if its window still doesn't open.
